title: speed-pitch-micro-account-cheat-deck-wip
summary: A compact, seller-facing slide kit and quick cheat-sheet for fast-moving small-mid deals. Focus: demo script, 3-minute pitch, objection lines, pilot success metrics, one-page technical checklist, and next-step templates.
body: TL;DR: 6 slides + 1 one-pager. Purpose: enable AE/SE to run a 10–20 minute micro-demo + close a pilot within a week. Keep latency/cost talking points super concrete. Emphasize fallback & predictable costs.

Slide 1 — Hook: 'Ship LLM features without a rewrite' bullets: 1) Same API across hosted/dedicated/private; 2) Predictable per-token economics for MVP; 3) Built-in fallbacks keep UX up during scale issues. Quick open: 30s customer problem statement (insert customer-specific line).

Slide 2 — Value props mapped to buyer roles: Product Manager: time-to-value (templates + SDKs). Platform/Infra: predictable throughput, reserved pools. Finance: cost-per-user math (example calc). Short callouts: "what success looks like in 30 days" for each role.

Slide 3 — Demo script (10 min): 0:00–0:45 intro + outcome; 0:45–3:00 run request through hosted API (show latency tokens/sec); 3:00–6:00 toggle to a cheaper quantized model and show cost delta; 6:00–9:00 show canary rollback via Console; 9:00–10:00 Q&A. Notes: keep data safe examples non-sensitive or use synthetic data.

Slide 4 — Objection playbook (quick cards): 'We don't want vendor lock-in' -> show same API & private deployment option; 'Costs are unpredictable' -> show batching + caching suggestions and per-route cost caps; 'SLA/Compliance' -> point to Private and Dedicated options + audit logs. Each objection: 1 sentence opener, 1 demo or artifact, 1 suggested next-step (pilot, SRE call, security checklist).

Slide 5 — Pilot template (week-by-week): Week0: scope + success metrics (latency P50/P95, cost per 1k requests, accuracy on sample prompts); Week1: onboarding + test harness; Week2: ramp to 10% traffic; Week3: evaluate metrics + expand or rollback. Shipping checklist: API keys, whitelist IPs, baseline eval dataset, fallback plan. Include a 6-line pilot SOW blurb for legal ops.

Slide 6 — Quick engineering checklist (one-pager): 1) Pin model version; 2) Configure batching threshold; 3) Enable prefix cache for repeated prompts; 4) Create fallback routing policy; 5) Add tracing hook to observability; 6) Set token budget per-route. Add sample commands: curl examples and SDK snippet placeholders (TODO: update before ship).

One-pager appendix — Pricing & fallback economics worked example: show 3 scenarios for 100k monthly requests: a) direct hosted (baseline), b) with caching (x% token reduction), c) dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit math). Keep numbers illustrative — callout: 'replace with customer telemetry during pilot'.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self): 1) Get latest per-token numbers from finance (Marcus). 2) Add short screen recording of canary rollback in Console (Jordana). 3) Replace SDK snippet with Go and Python minimal examples. 4) Validate legal SOW wording with contracts. 5) Create a one-click follow-up email template for AE to send after demo.

Suggested follow-up templates (short): Email subject: 'Quick pilot next steps — <account>' Body bullets: 1) links to sandbox API keys, 2) proposed pilot scope, 3) 30/60/90 outcomes, 4) ask for 1 technical POC + 1 business owner. Include calendar link and 'we'll run a 30-min tech handoff'.

Risk map (seller-facing): 1) Integration risk — mitigations: SDKs + sample app; 2) Cost surprise — mitigations: per-route caps + batching; 3) Quality regression — mitigations: eval harness, A/B rollout; 4) Ops burden — mitigations: Redwood Console + managed fallback. Short scripts per risk to read aloud during discovery.

Measurement: baseline metrics to capture during pilot: tokens/request, P50 latency, P95 latency, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, user-perceived failure rate (via synthetic probes). Suggest using our 'pilot dashboard' template (link in linked_artifacts).

Baseline scripts/commands (placeholder strings for SE): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"model":"rwd-compact-1","prompt":"<example>"}' — (NOTE: sanitize for customer demo).

Speaker notes / elevator lines: Keep to <= 3 sentences per slide. Example open: 'We help teams ship LLM features with predictable economics — not just a model, but the runtime + controls you need in production.' Close line: 'If you want predictable SLAs and to avoid surprise token bills, a scoped pilot is lowest friction next step.'

Appendix: competitor bullets (one-liners): 'Public LLM APIs: great for experimentation but unpredictable cost and noisy SLAs; cloud-managed endpoints: heavyweight infra ops; self-hosted: high ops burden. Redwood positioning: middle ground with predictable economics + optional private control plane.'

Distribution plan / enablement: 1) Run bake-off with 5 AEs this week (Marcus owns); 2) Capture two 10-min demo recordings and centralize in enablement folder (Jordana); 3) Weekly seller sync + friction log (Ethan to capture).

Notes-to-self: Keep this deck to single A4 when printed. Avoid deep architectural diagrams here — link to technical repo for platform details. Use concrete numbers and one-call-to-action: 'Start pilot'.
Contact & ownership: Asha Patel (owner) — asha@redwood.ai; Marcus Lee (pricing numbers); Jordana Ruiz (demo recording); Ethan Cho (pilot templates).
